name: Ben Horowitz

source.title: File:TechCrunch Disrupt San Francisco 2018 - day 2 (42713740520) (cropped).jpg — Wikimedia Commons

current_role: Co-founder and general partner of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)
summary: Ben Horowitz worked with Marc Andreessen at Netscape, co-founded Loudcloud (later Opsware, sold to Hewlett-Packard in 2007) and in 2009 co-founded the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz; he wrote The Hard Thing About Hard Things (2014). Son of conservative activist David Horowitz, he endorsed and funded Donald Trump in July 2024 alongside Andreessen, then in October 2024 pledged a significant donation to groups backing Kamala Harris. He and Andreessen are major funders of the pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future.

connections.name: Marc Andreessen
connections.description: Horowitz joined Andreessen at Netscape in 1995; they co-founded Loudcloud (later Opsware) in 1999 and the venture firm Andreessen Horowitz in 2009, and published its "Little Tech Agenda" and endorsed Trump together in July 2024.

sources.title: Andreessen Horowitz founders the latest to stake Trump — Fortune

connections.name: David Horowitz
connections.description: Father: the conservative activist and Freedom Center founder, who died in April 2025. Reporting describes the family's political split after David's turn to the right in the 1980s, and Ben's later, separate shift toward Republicans.

sources.title: Ben and Felicia Horowitz's political pivot from liberal darlings to Trump backers — Colorado Politics

connections.name: Donald Trump
connections.description: Horowitz endorsed Trump in July 2024 ("for little tech, we think Donald Trump is actually the right choice") and gave $2.5 million to the pro-Trump super PAC Right for America, per FEC filings. In October 2024 he told staff he and his wife would also make a significant donation to groups supporting Kamala Harris, citing friendship with her, while the firm stayed neutral.
